findings.evidence: Lines 88-100: the proof's only use of the two-sided hypothesis is `hγ.mono (Icc_subset_Icc (by linarith) le_rfl)` and `hγ.mono (Icc_subset_Icc le_rfl (by linarith))` — it immediately splits into the two halves and never relates them.
findings.fix: State it one-sided per side: `(hct : c < t) (htd : t < d) (hγL : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 γ (Icc c t)) (hγR : ContDiffOn ℝ 2 γ (Icc t d)) : HasLipschitzDerivOnEachSideAt γ t`. The existing proof body works verbatim with `Icc c t`/`Icc t d` in place of `Icc (t - ε) t`/`Icc t (t + ε)`; the two-sided `C²` case is then `hγ.mono` on each half at the call site.
findings.issue: `hasLipschitzDerivOnEachSideAt_of_contDiffOn` assumes `ContDiffOn ℝ 2 γ (Icc (t - ε) (t + ε))` — a symmetric window with the same regularity across `t` — while the sibling introduction lemma `hasLipschitzDerivOnEachSideAt_of_lipschitzOnWith` (line 75) takes arbitrary `c < t < d` with independent per-side data. A curve with a corner at `t` (the case this predicate was introduced for, per its own docstring at line 44) is not `C¹` across `t`, so it cannot use this lemma at all and must redo the `ContDiffOn.derivWithin` + `ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith` steps by hand.

findings.evidence: Lines 69-72: `calc |(z⁻¹ * v).im| ≤ ‖z⁻¹ * v‖ := Complex.abs_im_le_norm _` then `_ = ‖v‖ / ‖z‖ := by rw [norm_mul, norm_inv, mul_comm, ← div_eq_mul_inv]` — neither step mentions `hm` or `hz`; only the final `_ ≤ ‖v‖ / m := by gcongr` uses them. `norm_inv` holds unconditionally in a normed division ring, including at `z = 0`.
findings.fix: Prove `abs_realWindingIntegrand_le_div_norm {z v : ℂ} : |realWindingIntegrand z v| ≤ ‖v‖ / ‖z‖` (the existing first two calc steps, unchanged), and either drop the `m` form or keep it as a one-line corollary `(le_div_norm ..).trans (by gcongr)`. The single call site (`RealIntegral/OnCurve.lean:375`) already chains a `gcongr` step to `Cd / m`, so it can absorb the denominator comparison into that same step.
findings.issue: `abs_realWindingIntegrand_le_div_of_le_norm` assumes `0 < m` and `m ≤ ‖z‖`, but the first two calc steps already prove the hypothesis-free `|realWindingIntegrand z v| ≤ ‖v‖ / ‖z‖`, which also holds at `z = 0` (LHS `= |(0⁻¹ * v).im| = 0`, RHS `= ‖v‖ / 0 = 0`). The special case is proved directly instead of being derived from the general statement.

summary: Two new API lemmas carry hypotheses stronger than their proofs need: the C² introduction lemma for HasLipschitzDerivOnEachSideAt requires a symmetric two-sided C² window (excluding the corner case the predicate exists for), and the crude integrand bound bakes in a positive lower bound m that only the last calc step uses. Everything else sits at the natural level.
